summary.text: Alan Barron is the Family First candidate for South Barwon at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations, and also stood for the party there in 2022. His party page says he lives in Grovedale, retired in 2013 from the Australian Taxation Office, and has written three books on social and religious themes. He was earlier involved with the Call to Australia (Fred Nile) group and, in 2010, the DLP.

summary.text: Freya Hedley is standing for the Socialist Alliance in South Barwon at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a trans woman who works in tech support and hospitality, and she volunteers with a homelessness service in Geelong. Her party says she is active in campaigning for LGBTIQA+ rights and for Palestine.

priorities.text: I want to help my community rebuild solidarity with each other
Respect for diversity and human rights
Public funding so that everyone has an equal chance to reach their potential

summary.text: Izzy Scherrer is the Greens candidate for South Barwon at the 2026 Victorian election. She describes herself as a teacher, a women's health advocate and a community organiser, and the ABC adds that she works as a communications coordinator. In 2024 she ran for the City of Greater Geelong council in Deakin Ward and was not elected.

priorities.text: I'm passionate about creating a future where housing is affordable
Dependable public transport and properly funded public schools
Practical, achievable action on climate change
Politics rooted in the community and guided by evidence

summary.text: Josh Geard is One Nation's candidate for South Barwon at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC reports that he has spent more than 20 years in corporate roles in health care, which he says has shown him a health system in decline. Beyond that short note, no biography of him had been found when this profile was written in November 2026.

priorities.text: Fixing a health system he describes as crumbling

sources.title: South Barwon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Libby Pettit is the Liberal candidate for South Barwon at the 2026 Victorian election, having won preselection ahead of Geelong councillor Ron Nelson. According to the ABC, she was once a national champion runner and founded the fashion label Zerafima, which she still runs. She has degrees in both fashion marketing and optometry and earlier worked in design and production management.

occupation.text: Founder of the fashion brand Zerafima

sources.title: South Barwon: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Madilyn Gorman is the Victorian Socialists candidate for South Barwon at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in mental health and social work and has spent close to two decades in the public health system, where she has been a union delegate and sat on a union branch committee. She grew up in Geelong and came back to the area to bring up her two children. In 2022 she led the party's Legislative Council ticket in Western Victoria Region.

occupation.text: Mental health worker and social worker

prior_roles.role: Union delegate and branch committee member
prior_roles.note: Her sources don't say whether she still holds these positions.

Affordable housing, public transport, schools and health services for a fast-growing area
Aged care and childcare run by the public sector
More hospital beds and more staff in health care
Smaller classes and more schools, so children with extra needs are not left out

summary.text: Rebecca Thistleton is Labor's candidate for South Barwon at the 2026 Victorian election. A former journalist who started out at local community papers, she now heads the Victorian arm of the McKell Institute, a policy think tank. She stood for Labor in the seat of Melbourne in 2022. Her party page says she lives in Armstrong Creek with her husband and their two children.

occupation.text: Head of the McKell Institute in Victoria (policy think tank); former journalist

prior_roles.role: Leads the McKell Institute in Victoria

priorities.text: Good schools, health care and local services that keep up with South Barwon's growth

summary.text: Ron Nelson, a sitting councillor on the City of Greater Geelong, is standing as an independent in South Barwon at the 2026 Victorian election. His campaign site says he has been on the council for more than 14 years and has twice served as deputy mayor, most recently from 2024 to 2026. He was the Liberal candidate for Bellarine in 2014 and later lost a Liberal preselection contest for South Barwon to Libby Pettit. Before local government he was a chef and small-business owner and worked in procurement for the Department of Defence.

occupation.text: Local councillor; previously a chef and small-business owner

prior_roles.note: His campaign site says he has been deputy mayor twice; Wikipedia's list gives his latest term as 2024 to 2026. The years of the earlier term aren't published.

prior_roles.role: Disability services and workplace-injury recovery support

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's candidate list for this election labels him Liberal but gives no result for the ward; his campaign site says he has won five consecutive Greater Geelong council elections.
Wikipedia's results table labels him an Independent Liberal.

priorities.text: We need less taxes, not more.
Safer intersections, road projects finished on time and better public transport linking local suburbs
A secondary school in Mount Duneed, which he says he has sought for years
Holding the government to the promised ambulance and fire stations at Armstrong Creek
Representing the electorate without being bound to a party
